_comment: CLAY, STAGE TWO (#115). Grog is a NON-PLASTIC TEMPER - it controls shrinkage and thermal shock
and actively reduces plasticity, which is the opposite of what a clay body needs. The plasticity
has to come from an actual clay mineral, and the standard fix for a body that comes out 'short'
is bentonite. Which is what clumping cat litter is.
So the two halves are useless apart and correct together, and that is why both are in the chain.
Dry-blending before adding water is real practice rather than a concession to the interface,
which is what makes this step honest instead of a workaround.
